item.title: Houston TCG Con X
item.description:

💥 Houston… Round X: From one to ten – What a pull it’s been! 🎉 🎴 Three Days • FREE Entry • 100+ Vendors • Nonstop Trades! What started as a small weekend card show has turned into a full-on collector movement. Houston TCG Con is back at CCS with Round X: a full 3-day weekend built on trades, collecting, and community. More time to dig. More time to trade. More time to find something you didn’t even know you needed. 🃏🤝   📅 Date: August 7-9, 2026 ⏰ Time: Friday: 3PM – 10PM | Saturday: 10AM – 6PM | Sunday: 10AM – 5PM 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St, #1500, Houston, TX 77036 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking!   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 🃏 100+ TCG Vendors — The Houston Trade Floor Shop from 100+ curated vendors from across Texas and beyond. Tables will be stacked with: ✅ Top titles including Pokémon, Magic: The Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh!, One Piece, Lorcana, Digimon, Weiss Schwarz, and more. ✅ Sealed product + booster boxes ✅ Graded slabs + collector singles ✅ Binder deals + playable staples ✅ Japanese imports + hard-to-find pickups ✅ Sleeves, top loaders, storage & accessories   ⚡ Buy • Sell • Trade — All Weekend This is what Houston TCG Con is known for. Bring your binders, make the deals you’ve been waiting for, and connect with collectors. This is where grails change hands and collections level up.   🔍 On-Site Grading Submissions & Card Restorations — Cappy’s Cards! Have a card you’ve been thinking about grading? Or one that needs a little restoration? Cappy’s Cards will be on-site helping collectors with grading submissions, restoration services, and expert insight all weekend.   🤝 Built by the Community — 10 Rounds Strong From first packs opened around the kitchen table to the cards you still chase today, this is where it all comes back. The trades, the stories, the people you meet along the way, Round X is a milestone for everyone who grew up with the hobby and never really left it. Bring your crew (and your binder) and relive it with us. Houston TCG Con X is back for a bigger weekend, with the same community that’s always made it feel like home.   🎨 Face Painting Fun | Saturday Step away from the tables and add some extra style to your TCG Con experience with fun face painting designs. ✨ By @will.and.whimsy   💼 Vendors – Claim Your Spot! item.title: Welcome to the Ion: An Introduction and Tour
item.description:
Friday, August 7, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Join the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, Wade Pinder, for an engaging tour and introduction to the Ion, Houston’s dynamic hub for innovation and entrepreneurship, powered by Rice University. This event is designed for entrepreneurs, students, professionals, investors, community leaders, and anyone curious about what the Ion has to offer. For those new to Houston and eager to connect with the local innovation ecosystem, this event provides the perfect opportunity to get started. The tour will begin in the lobby at 10:00 AM and conclude at 11:00 AM. During this time, participants will learn about the Ion’s resources, events, and facilities. Highlights of the tour include the technology showcases, coworking spaces, public areas, and the on-site restaurants and bars. About Wade Pinder Wade Pinder is a dedicated advocate for Houston’s innovation community, serving as the Ion’s Mentor in Residence. With a wealth of experience in product management, community building, and fostering entrepreneurial growth, Wade offers invaluable insights into how the Ion serves as a launchpad for ideas and innovation. The Vision of the Ion Powered by Rice University, the Ion is the epicenter of the 16-acre innovation district in the heart of Houston’s midtown. Committed to being the home for Houston’s innovation community, the Ion District propels the transformative culture of people, places, ideas, and experiences that build a better quality of life for all of Houston. The Ion is a beautifully restored building at 4201 Main Street. It connects Houston’s talent, academic, corporate, and entrepreneurial communities in a collaborative environment designed to inspire and grow ideas. The Ion serves as a space where serendipitous collisions lead to meaningful connections and opportunities. What to Expect Coworking Spaces: Explore flexible work areas tailored for collaboration and creativity. Public Spaces: Discover spaces designed for networking, inspiration, and community events. Restaurants and Bars: Experience the on-site dining options that make the Ion a lively hub. Through its programs and partnerships, the Ion empowers individuals and organizations to build, solve, and innovate. From prototyping to pitching, accelerating to sustaining, the Ion is Houston’s headquarters for turning ideas into reality. Whether you have a promising product, an intriguing technology, a budding business idea, or are simply curious about the Ion and its offerings, this tour will provide valuable insights into how the Ion can help connect your “What-ifs” with “What now.” Don’t miss this opportunity to explore and be inspired by Houston’s innovation ecosystem.

From Ion District

Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: Daniel Sloss: BITTER LIVE at The Wilbur (Matinee)
item.description:
Sunday, August 9, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: The Wilbur, 246 Tremont St., Boston, MA, 2116

Official TicketsResale Tickets About the Performer Daniel Sloss is one of Scotland’s most celebrated stand-up comedians, known for his razor-sharp wit, dark humor, and deeply personal storytelling. He first gained international attention with his Netflix specials Dark and Jigsaw, the latter of which became famous for reportedly causing thousands of breakups worldwide after audiences reconsidered their relationships. Now Sloss is back with his brand-new tour, BITTER — a show that dives headfirst into love, loss, and the messy aftermath of both. Expect the same unflinching honesty and comedic brilliance that has made him one of the most talked-about comedians of his generation. His style blends laugh-out-loud moments with genuine emotional depth, leaving audiences both in stitches and in their feelings. Event Details Date: Sunday, August 9, 2026 Time: 3:00 PM (Matinee Show) Venue: The Wilbur, 246 Tremont St, Boston, MA 02116 Doors Open: Approximately 2:00 PM Age Restriction: 18+ recommended (adult content) Ticket Prices: From $68 (avg. ~$147) About the Venue The Wilbur is one of Boston’s most iconic and beloved comedy venues, located in the heart of the Theatre District at 246 Tremont Street. Built in 1914, this stunning 1,200-seat theater combines historic elegance with modern amenities, offering an intimate yet grand atmosphere perfect for stand-up comedy. The venue features excellent sightlines from every seat, a full bar, and a warm, energetic atmosphere that makes every show feel special. Whether you’re in the orchestra, mezzanine, or balcony, you’ll feel close to the action. Parking is available at nearby garages, and the venue is easily accessible via the MBTA Green and Orange Lines (Boylston and Back Bay stations). What to Expect This is a rare Sunday matinee performance of Daniel Sloss’s BITTER tour — a perfect afternoon outing for comedy fans who want to experience one of the world’s best stand-up comedians in an intimate Boston setting. The show runs approximately 90 minutes with no intermission. Sloss performs solo, commanding the stage with his signature blend of dark comedy and personal narrative. Fans of his Netflix specials will find BITTER to be his most mature and emotionally resonant work yet. Come prepared to laugh hard, think deeply, and leave with a new perspective on relationships and life. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. item.title: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas Showcase (Early)
item.description:
Monday, August 10, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino, 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV, 89103, United States

This post contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: Mercury Fund Day at the Ion: AI Product Design and Distribution: Lessons from Building at Scale
item.description:
Tuesday, August 11, 2026 at 3:30 PM

Location: Ion – Forum Stairs, 4201 Main St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Welcome to “Mercury Fund Day at the Ion” – a program series hosted by the Ion and Mercury, where software founders can connect with mentorship at Houston’s HQ for innovation. What is it: Mercury Fund Day, previously known as Software Day, is a monthly series driving the support, inspiration, and connections needed to help startups on their path to rapid, sustainable growth. Each month, Mercury Fund Day will include office hours (by application), a keynote session, and networking. Each month will include a new speaker and topic covering the latest trends and breakthroughs in software technology and practical advice for founders. From AI to blockchain and guidance on fundraising, explore topics that are relevant for your company’s journey. Afterward, join us for a networking happy hour at Second Draught, brought to you by Gunderson Dettmer, where you can connect with fellow entrepreneurs, investors, and industry professionals, forging connections that could shape the future of your venture. This month’s topic: Every enterprise software company says it’s going AI-first. Few have actually rebuilt the product, the pricing model, and the team around it. Join us at Mercury Day at Ion Houston on August 11th for a working conversation with three people doing that rebuild from different seats: Mustafa Ali (Growth, Twilio), Zafir Khan (Product, Meta), and Salim Gheewalla (Founder, Utilitise, which replaced the IT help desk with AI that fixes problems before anyone notices). Panelists will get into what separates a great AI product experience from a clunky one, when AI should run invisibly in the background versus prompt the user directly, what consumption-based pricing does to a SaaS business model, and how hiring changes when a team is building AI-native from day one. Hosted by Heath Butler of Mercury Fund, panelists include: Mustafa Ali – Growth @ Twilio Zafir Khan – Product @ Meta (former Mercury Intern) Salim Gheewalla – Founder @ Utilitise Prior to the fireside chat, a select group of early-stage software startups will participate in office hours. Over the course of 2-hours, first-time entrepreneurs looking for guidance or seasoned founders needing help tackling tough challenges will have access to a group of curated mentors from the Mercury network and gain insights and guidance tailored to their needs. Startups are invited to apply to participate here by Tuesday, August 4. “Mercury Fund Day at the Ion” isn’t just an event – it’s a catalyst for growth and collaboration. Don’t miss this opportunity to be part of Houston’s thriving tech ecosystem. Join us as we bring together leading mentors, promising startups, and like-minded Houstonians focused on transformative software innovations.  

From Ion District

item.title: Lunchtime Learning (Virtual)
item.description:
Wednesday, August 12, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Zoom

Virtual Lunchtime Learning sponsored by the Committee on the Environment (COTE)   First Safe, then Circular: optimizing material health with Cradle to Cradle Certified® If you are being asked to evaluate the material health of products and aren’t sure where to start, this session is for you! We’ll dive into the basics of material health for designers, including major classes of chemicals of concern, chemical assessments, and how designers can use certifications as they evaluate products. This presentation details the methodology and requirements for the Cradle to Cradle Certified® products program and how designers can use it to specify materials that are healthy in a project and across a supply chain. We’ll explore how Cradle to Cradle Certified®, as a fully digitized program, makes it easy for designers to find reliable material health information to deliver meaningful sustainability benefits on every project.   Speaker: Ren DeCherney, Director of Built Environment Ren is a licensed interior designer who uses her first-hand experience of the complexities of the building industry to help designers and manufacturers translate their sustainability pledges into reality. Prior to joining the Institute as Director of Built Environment, she worked in Portland as a designer, where she took her firm PVC-free, making them the first firm in Portland to make such a commitment. She was then the Director of Industry Transparency at Source, a digital materials platform, where she synthesized design team needs and industry trends to integrate sustainability seamlessly into the design process. This included building various user tools, growing strategic partnerships, and developing all of the sustainability filters on the platform. She then worked at the International Living Future Institute, overseeing the Declare and Living Product Challenge programs. There she worked with both designers and manufacturers to understand the current market incentives for sustainable practices and how to implement sustainability strategy into everyday practices.   AIA Credit: 1.0 HSW GBCI Credit: self-report

item.title: Jesus Benavente: NUESTROWORLD
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks, @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd & Various Locations, 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX, 77011, United States

Opening Thursday, August 13, 2026 | 6 – 8 pm DiverseWorks @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd NUESTROWORLD is a satirical solo installation by Brooklyn-based artist Jesus Benavente. Featuring newly commissioned works, NuestroWorld opens on Thursday, August 13, 2026, transforming 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX 77011 into a fictional visitor center for NuestroWorld, encouraging guests to explore Houston beyond the gallery walls and experience the city as an amusement park. The installation will be on view through September 13, 2026, with a closing party on September 11. Gallery hours are Thursday – Saturday, 12 – 6 pm. Admission is free. Through satire and spectacle, NuestroWorld examines how cities construct identity through tourism, branding, memory, and myth, inviting audiences to reconsider Houston’s past and present. The exhibition draws inspiration from pivotal moments in Houston and Texas history, including the opening of the Astrodome and Astroworld in the late 1960s, Selena’s iconic Houston Livestock Show & Rodeo performances in the 1990s, and the folklore surrounding Santa Anna’s capture following the Battle of San Jacinto in 1836, highlighting the city’s recurring cycles of ambition, folly, and heartbreak. The title plays on “Astroworld” and uses Spanglish to create the phrase “The World Is Ours,” reframing Houston’s cultural mythology through humor, nostalgia, and critical reflection. Opening Reception Thursday, August 13, 6 – 8 pm Artist and Curator Talk: 6:45 pm Closing Party Friday, September 11, 2026, 6 – 8 pm 7 pm: special performance by CTS Trio – Queen of Tejano & Latin Tribute ARTIST BIO: Jesus Benavente is a visual artist based in Brooklyn, New York, and born in San Antonio, Texas. Benavente earned an MFA from Rutgers University and attended Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture. Recent exhibitions and performances include Reception Rome, Italy; the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York; Queens Museum; LTD Los Angeles; Performa 13, New York; Acre Projects, Chicago; Chinati Foundation, Marfa; the Neuberger Museum of Art, Purchase, NY; Shin Museum of Art, South Korea; Vox Populi, Philadelphia; and Socrates Sculpture Park, New York. Website: http://jesusbenavente.net Instagram: @testotesto3  

From DiverseWorks

item.title: Everyday Self-Defense: Building Confidence Through Boundaries & De-escalation
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 5 PM

Location: Third Ward Jiu-Jitsu, 2016 Emancipation Ave, Houston, TX, 77003, United States

In this self-defense session, the instructor, Sarah Degar, Jiu Jitsu black belt, and architect at GSMA, will share her unique approach to personal safety, focusing on two key objectives: setting boundaries and de-escalating potential uncomfortable situations. After demonstrating key techniques, attendees will partner up to practice, with the instructor offering guidance to each group. The first part of the session will teach participants how to navigate unwanted physical contact in everyday situations, particularly with people they know. In professional and social contexts, it can be challenging to assert boundaries—especially for many women who already worry about being perceived as “unreasonable.” The instructor will address simple strategies to divert this contact to maintain comfort and autonomy. For example, a colleague approaches for a hug or puts an arm around the waist to pose for a photo. Attendees will be empowered to practice subtle yet effective ways to establish personal space without confrontation. The second part of the session will address more serious scenarios, where the potential for physical harm exists. Whether the concern comes from someone familiar or not, de-escalation is crucial. Participants will learn techniques to create and maintain a safe distance, keep a steady stance to avoid being easily pushed or pulled, and how to break free from various types of holds. The session will wrap up with interactive games designed to reinforce the skills learned, making it fun and memorable while encouraging participants to continue practicing on their own. Doors Open 5p Class 5:30p – 6:30p Social to follow Advanced Registration Required.  

From AIA Houston

item.title: The future of engineering from Anthropic’s Eng Service Co CTO
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Zoom

Register here: https://luma.com/8q74pmn4 AI has changed what it means to be an engineer. As GenAI models become capable of tackling increasingly complex work, the value that engineers bring is changing: deciding what should be built, designing reliable systems, validating AI-generated work, understanding customers, and orchestrating agents. The changes are accelerating. What does this mean for engineers in the future, and how does one stay relevant? Join Eddie Siegel, Co-Founder & CTO of Ode, Anthropic’s engineering services company, for a candid, unscripted conversation about where engineering is heading, what skills will matter over the next decade, and how to cultivate and deploy them. Before Anthropic, Eddie built engineering organizations at LiveRamp, Wove, Samba TV, Xip, and Fractional AI. Through Fractional AI, he worked inside dozens of engineering teams deploying production AI systems, giving him a front-row seat to what actually changes when AI moves from ad hoc assistance to firm-wide transformation. Today, Ode is building for that future, executing gargantuan transformative projects yielding millions of dollars for fortune 100 companies. Topics we’ll explore: – Where AI is heading, from Anthropic model capabilities to organizational transformation – Where engineering is heading, and what it means to stay competitive – What Ode is doing, why it’s growing so quickly, and a look behind the scenes – Who Ode is hiring and what the firm is looking for to execute under Anthropic – Your questions Who Should Attend: This event is for software engineers, engineering leaders, founders, computer and data scientists, and anyone thinking seriously about their place in an AI-native future. Whether you’re trying to future-proof your career, understand where engineering is heading, or explore opportunities to build the next generation of developer tools, this conversation is for you. Expect an open conversation about where engineering is going and the people who will shape what’s next.

item.title: Hands-On Workshop: Build Your Own Reusable AI System
item.description:
Friday, August 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/hands-on-workshop-build-your-own-reusable-ai-system-tickets-1995123296487?aff=oddtdtcreator Most AI advice focuses on clever prompts. This workshop gives you a solid tool you will use again and again. At this month’s Social Media Breakfast Houston, Kami Huyse and Jennifer Texada will show you how to stop starting from scratch every time you sit down with AI. In the first half hour, they’ll break down what a Smart Card is and why it turns scattered prompting into a repeatable system. Then it’s build time! You’ll build one yourself, live, with guidance every step of the way. You’ll leave with a working Smart Card built for your own work, ready to use right away with the AI tool of your choice. Choose to create a tool that will help you build your monthly newsletter, proposals, client reports, a press release, or something else you do regularly and would like a repeatable process to help with. This session is hands-on. Bring a laptop and an AI tool that lets you upload files, such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Microsoft Copilot. We’ll walk through how to start a project on ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini. Bring a real task you want AI to help with. What you will learn: How to spot and create a repeatable process you can hand off to AI. What AI should do and what humans should keep control of. How to organize your data and content so you aren’t trapped in one tool. Why it’s worth creating a reusable Project, GPT, or Gem instead of starting over each time. When it makes sense to use the desktop version of your AI tool. How to set up a project in ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini so your Smart Card is ready to use.

item.description:
Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 9 AM

Location: The Lighthouse of Houston, 3602 West Dallas, Houston, TX, 77019, United States

Join us at The Lighthouse of Houston on August 15 from 9:00 AM to 12:30 PM for our 2026 Transition and Resource Fair—a dynamic, hands-on event designed for blind and visually impaired youth ages 14–22. This exciting fair empowers students with essential life skills including self-advocacy, confidence building, job readiness, and computer literacy. Attendees will explore adaptive technology, orientation and mobility training, and even get creative with accessible arts and crafts. The event also features a wide range of community and government resources—all at no cost. Plus, students will receive free BVI accessible school supplies and a backpack! item.title: Retro Video Game Expo III
item.description:
Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 10 AM

🕹️ Houston, Press Start on a Weekend of Pure Retro Nostalgia! 👾 Step back into the golden era of gaming at Retro Video Game Expo III, a two-day celebration of classic consoles, arcade legends, competitive retro tournaments, and nonstop free play. From expanded free-play zones spanning the 80s and beyond to live, high-energy tournament matchups and a collector-focused marketplace, this expo is built for gamers who chase high scores and grail finds.   🗓️ Date & Time: August 15–16, 2026 | 10AM–5PM 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St #1500, Houston, TX 77036 💥 FREE ENTRY. FREE PARKING. FREE PLAY.   🎮 Event Highlights 🎮 Retro Video Game Marketplace – All Weekend Step into a collector’s paradise. Vendors from across the region are bringing vintage consoles, original cartridges, imports, manuals, accessories, and hard-to-find titles. This is where treasures respawn. 🚨 Want to vend? Sign up here 👉 https://tinyurl.com/HoustonVendors   👾 Free-Play Zone – Both Days | ALL Day Jump on 80’s Arcades & Classic Consoles and relive the games that made gaming legendary. More setups and activities to be announced soon!   🎸 Retro Video Game Music: One-Man Live Show – Saturday & Sunday | 12PM–2PM Take a break from the consoles and jam out to a live solo performance of your favorite video game soundtracks. Bust some dance moves to guitar and keyboard covers of classic tracks from Sega, Super Mario Bros., Metal Gear Solid, Street Fighter II & III, Tekken 3, Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy, Tetris, Rayxanber II, and more. ✨ Hosted by @Voe2pt0   🕹️ Retro Madness Gaming Station – Both Days | All Day Free play? All day. Challenge your friends to a round of classic GameCube titles. Prefer GTA or Minecraft? They’re here too! Grab a controller and play as long as you want! ✨ Hosted by @hunnypotproject   🃏 UNO Tournament – Saturday | 12PM–5PM Get ready for fast-paced UNO action! Join Kung Fu Eddy for a tournament filled with strategy, surprises, and friendly competition. Players will battle through rounds using classic UNO rules with special twists, including advanced rules, UNO Flip semifinals, and a mystery deck championship match. Don’t want to compete? A casual play table will be available for anyone who wants to jump in and have fun! ✨ Hosted by @kungfueddybaybee   🏨 Special Hotel Deals Enjoy a special rate of $79/night — 2 Queens at TownePlace Suites, only 15 minutes away from the action! Book your stay 👉🏻 https://www.marriott.com/event-reservations/reservation-link.mi?id=1767823967549&key=CORP&app=resvlink   Bring your crew, grab a controller, and let’s relive the golden age of gaming together. 👾

item.title: Froggy Night
item.description:
Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 7 PM

$37 member / $52 nonmemberInstructor: Dr. Cassidy Johnson Ages 21+ Hop on over for a wet, wild night! Enjoy refreshments (frog-themed snacks, coffee, and Saint Arnold Brewing Company beer) while you learn all about the strange and wonderful world of frogs, from their croaking courtship to their mysterious metamorphosis. Weather permitting, we’ll also go for a hike to search for frogs and other nocturnal creatures. Please dress for the weather and wear walking shoes. register online Instructor bio: Dr. Cassidy Johnson has a B.S. and M.S. in Biology at Texas A&M University – Corpus Christi and a Ph.D. in Biochemistry & Cell Biology from Rice University. She loves teaching biology and is currently an Assistant Teaching Professor for Rice BioSciences. She fell in love with local amphibians while working for the Houston toad ex situ conservation program at the Houston Zoo. She is also passionate about the protection and restoration of Texas prairies and is on the board of the Native Prairie Association of Texas and was previously the president of the Coastal Prairie Partnership.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Spiritual Resolve for Fearless Living at Eternal Gandhi Museum Houston
item.description:
Sunday, August 16, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Eternal Gandhi Museum Houston, 12379 Riceville School Rd, Houston, 77031, United States

Self Enquiry Life Fellowship presents Spiritual Resolve for Fearless Living: Guided Meditation & Lecture by Himalayan Monk, HH Swami Vidyadhishananda at Eternal Gandhi Museum Houston. His Holiness Swami Vidyadhishananda, a Himalayan monk and Sanskritist, will lead a sacred Sunday morning centered on the theme of spiritual resilience and resolve amidst unstable times. Through direct experience of guided meditation, along with words of wisdom and spiritual advice, guests will take home meaningful guidance about spiritual resolve and resilience amidst the challenges and the difficult times ahead. The fellowship invites all to discover the steady ground of spiritual wisdom and contemplative practice, timeless anchors that hold firm through any challenge. The morning will open with sublime Sanskrit chanting by His Holiness, followed by guided meditation, words of wisdom, a blessing line, and more. A light Vegetarian lunch will be provided in the foyer during the blessing line. Doors at 9:30am. Admission Tickets are $15. item.title: The Technology Leadership Advantage Series
item.description:
Tuesday, August 18, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/1995696286315?aff=oddtdtcreator Technology Isn’t Your Competitive Advantage Anymore. Leadership Is. Why High-Growth Companies Win Long Before They Write Another Line of Code Technology has never been more powerful or more accessible. Cloud infrastructure, enterprise software, AI models, development tools, and specialized technical capabilities that once separated companies are now available to almost everyone. Yet companies with access to remarkably similar technology continue to produce very different results. The difference is increasingly leadership. As companies grow, technology decisions stop being purely technical decisions. They become decisions about growth, capital, customers, product direction, risk, organizational design, and competitive position. And the leadership model that helped a company reach one stage of growth may not be the leadership model it needs for the next. Join Ram Prasad, CEO of Delence, for an executive conversation about where competitive advantage is moving and why high-growth companies need to build technology leadership before growth exposes the gap. This isn’t a technical presentation about tools, platforms, or the latest AI trend. It’s a conversation about leadership, growth, technology, and the decisions that shape enterprise value. What We’ll Discuss Why access to technology is becoming less differentiated Why leadership and judgment become more valuable as technology becomes more accessible How growth changes what companies need from technology leadership Why organizations can add engineers, platforms, and tools without improving execution Why companies sometimes outgrow the leadership model that got them here Why AI creates an executive leadership challenge, not simply a technology opportunity How strong technology leadership connects business strategy, product, technology, AI, and execution How to recognize leadership gaps before they become growth constraints Who Should Attend This session is specifically designed for CEOs, seeded startup founders, presidents, investors, private equity leaders, operating partners, and board members of growth-stage B2B technology and technology-enabled companies. It will be particularly relevant if your organization is experiencing rapid growth, increasing technology complexity, product scaling challenges, AI investment, or questions about whether the current leadership structure is ready for the next stage. If technology decisions are increasingly becoming CEO, board, investment, or growth decisions, this conversation is for you. One Question to Consider Before You Arrive Is your leadership team built for the next three years and not the last three? About Ram Prasad Ram Prasad is CEO of Delence and an executive technology leader focused on the intersection of technology, product, AI, and business growth. Throughout his corporate career, Ram has worked with executive teams navigating the decisions that emerge as organizations grow when technology becomes more complex, product priorities compete, AI creates new possibilities, and decisions that were once technical begin affecting growth, risk, and enterprise value. His perspective is built around a simple idea: Growth has a leadership problem. Ram speaks and advises on executive technology leadership, AI strategy, product strategy, scaling, and the leadership decisions that turn technology into business advantage. About Delence Delence provides executive technology leadership to growth-stage B2B technology and technology-enabled companies. Through Fractional CAIO, CTO and CPO leadership, Delence works alongside CEOs and executive teams when the business needs senior technology, product, or AI leadership, but a permanent executive hire may not yet be the right answer. Delence connects business strategy, technology, product, AI, and execution, bringing executive ownership to the decisions that become more consequential as companies grow. This isn’t staffing or recruiting. It is executive leadership for the stage the business is entering.

From Ion District

item.description:

Join us for the third session of the EP University Lecture Series: Project Delivery. All architecture projects have fundamentally followed the same processes from programming, to design, to documentation and construction. This course reveals the step-by-step process in delivering a project from conception to reality. Review the phases of design – Programming, Site Planning, Schematic Design, and Design Development – to understand the processes and deliverables for each phase Understand the project team member roles – internal and external – and how projects move from person to person and phase to phase Understand the process of developing construction documents to execute the design vision – from cartoon set, to establishing what to draw, why to draw it, and what team members are responsible for confirming constructability and details Review the process of formally issuing drawings including sealing documents, labelling drawings, permitting documents, transmitting drawings and handling drawing revisions Presented by Jeanette Shaw of Powers Brown Architecture, this session offers 1LU CE credit.  Lunch is provided. item.title: Concrete Cosmos: Composing Skate Architecture
item.description:
Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: TX

In Concrete Cosmos: Composing Skate Architecture, Shane Yee presents skate architecture qua architecture, framing the skatepark as a paradigmatic yet unacknowledged achievement of the contemporary moment, characterized by adaptive reuse, the blurring of public and private space, an emphasis on lifestyle recreation, and the ascent of subcultural practices into mainstream culture. Skate spaces manifest in fluid, naturalistic configurations, converging with land art and anticipating parametric/ digital aesthetics; yet despite this sophistication, the language and principles of the discipline remain largely unarticulated. Drawing on a half-century history of skatepark design (1976-2026) and his own work at Skate Ecosystems, Yee offers a chronological series of architectural close readings, examining design intentions, ordering logics, and formal arrangements. The lecture establishes skate architecture as an emergent field with significant cultural, spatial, and spiritual implications, capable of producing elevated human experiences. About Shane Yee Shane Yee earned his Bachelor of Architecture degree from NewSchool of Architecture & Design in San Diego, California. Mr. Yee has a broad range of experiences and capabilities in all phases of project planning, design and construction- from acquisition through operations and maintenance. He has designed award-winning projects including residential, multifamily, civic, religious, master planning, and of course, skate spaces. As an officer in the United States Navy Civil Engineer Corps, Mr. Yee expertly designed & managed DOD projects with a total value of 100+ million to include Design-Build, DBB, and MILCON construction. Mr. Yee is a member of the American Institute of Architects, Society of American Military Engineers, and US Green Building Council.   This program is in conjunction with Kinetics of Urban Movement, on view at the Architecture Center Houston from June 18-September 26. Exhibition Sponsors and Community Partners Kinetics of Urban Movement is funded in part by the City of Houston through Houston Arts Alliance Cherries Wheels Honey Skate Club Houston Parks and Recreation Department Houston Skate Academy Select Skate ECOSYSTEMS Southside Skatepark

item.title: How to Start a Startup
item.description:
Wednesday, August 19, 2026 at 5 PM

Location: Ion – Forum Stairs, 4201 Main St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

You have an idea…now what? Before you start looking for funding, it’s important to ensure that your idea is both viable and valuable — if it doesn’t have a sound model and a market willing to pay for it, investors won’t be interested anyway. Join us after the session, hosted by Heath Butler, for a networking happy hour! Target Audience: Startups and Entrepreneurs: early-stage entrepreneurs, entrepreneurs testing ideas for a pivot Community Members: people with an idea for a startup but unsure what to do next, small business owners Corporate Innovators: intrapreneurs, decision-makers tasked with creating and leading sustainable change Academic Partners: students or faculty with an idea for a startup About the Speakers: Heath Butler, Mercury Fund Heath focuses on B2B SaaS and B2B2C Marketplace investments in future-of-work and fin-tech themes. Heath also manages the organization’s venture studio and network platform, including corporate, service provider, and startup community relationships. Prior to joining Mercury, Heath co-founded Gestalt Theory Venture Partners, a venture studio and angel investing group. Prior to Gestalt, Heath held leadership roles as a seasoned go-to-market and corporate development executive at Insperity (NYSE: NSP), the nation’s leading HR outsourcing services provider. Prior to Insperity, Heath led business development for EnergyWorkspace.com, founded a fin-tech startup, and developed his foundational management skills at UPS. Outside of Mercury, Heath is an active angel investor and advocates for democratizing access to private equity opportunities for all investors. He is an active startup in the Houston innovation community, a mentor, and a regular speaker/mentor within The Ion. Heath enjoys traveling with family and likes to read, golf, cycle, and is an avid poker player.

item.title: Park Conversations: Remembering and Honoring the Soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment
item.description:
Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: Clay Family Eastern Glades, 6500 Memorial Dr, Houston, TX, 77007, United States

Join us for a free audio story exhibit at Clay Family Eastern Glades Beginning August 20, Memorial Park Conservancy and the Buffalo Soldiers National Museum invite the public to Clay Family Eastern Glades for the annual return of our historic interactive audio installation, Park Conversations: Remembering and Honoring the Soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment. The exhibit will be available to experience on-site through September 27. Can’t make it to the exhibit? All stories are available online. Click Here to learn more and listen now. The history of Memorial Park and Camp Logan Before Memorial Park, the land was Camp Logan – a U.S. Army training camp built in the spring of 1917, just weeks after the United States entered World War I. That summer, African American soldiers of the 3rd Battalion, 24th Infantry Regiment, one of the Army’s four “Buffalo Soldiers” regiments, arrived to guard the camp’s construction. In the aftermath of the tragedy on August 23, 1917, the battalion was disarmed and transferred. What followed was the largest court-martial in American military history, resulting in the execution of 19 soldiers and life sentences for 63 others. That verdict stood until November 13, 2023, when the U.S. Army formally set aside the convictions of all 110 soldierstried in the case. The Army also committed to correcting the soldiers’ service records, making their descendants eligible for benefits their families had been denied for a century.   Exhibit Details: Presented in partnership with the Buffalo Soldiers National Museum, the installation uses onsite audio stories to bring this history to life throughout Clay Family Eastern Glades. Where: Clay Family Eastern Glades, 552 East Memorial Loop Drive, Houston, TX 77007 When: August 20 – September 27 Cost: Free and open to the public Bring headphones. The audio is designed for personal, uninterrupted listening Parking: Paid parking available onsite at a rate of $2 for 3 hours. Free parking is available in adjacent lots.

item.title: Mapping Houston's Innovation Ecosystem
item.description:
Friday, August 21, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 027, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002

Facilitated by Wade Pinder, Ion’s Mentor in Residence Houston’s startup and innovation ecosystem is as vast and dynamic as the city itself, full of opportunities, resources, and talent. Yet, navigating it can be challenging—especially for those unfamiliar with its many parts. Whether you’re an entrepreneur, investor, educator, student, community leader or curious professional, this session will offer valuable insights into how Houston’s innovation ecosystem works and how you can find your place within it. Discover the Houston Ecosystem’s Flow Facilitated by Wade Pinder, the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, this session will help participants map out the journey needed to take an idea from concept to a mature company. Wade brings years of experience in product management, community building, and mentoring entrepreneurs to the table, offering a thoughtful and informed perspective to guide this exploration. The heart of the session lies in exploring a dynamic mind map that Wade has created and continues to refine—an ever-evolving, community-driven tool that grows alongside Houston’s innovation ecosystem. Attendees will not only learn about the ecosystem’s flow but also have the opportunity to contribute to it by identifying gaps, sharing knowledge, and adding their insights. This session will center on the stages of a company’s growth journey, exploring the essential elements that drive it forward. Participants will examine the role of financial capital, from early fundraising efforts to securing the resources needed for scaling, and how these milestones align with a company’s progression. The discussion will also delve into the human element of growing a business, highlighting the evolving talent and expertise required to navigate the entrepreneurial journey. Additionally, we’ll explore the importance of “social capital”—the networks, support systems, and relationships that play a critical role in moving ideas to market and sustaining long-term growth. Ion’s Vision Helping the community better understand the local ecosystem reflects the Ion’s commitment “to being the home for Houston’s innovation community.” By fostering connections, creating opportunities, and sharing perspectives, the Ion is building a transformative culture that strengthens Houston’s economic resiliency and celebrates the entrepreneurial journey. From forming an initial entrepreneurial idea to the prototyping phase to scaling a business, this Houston Ecosystem Mapping session aligns with the Ion’s goals to support innovation, attract talent, and build a vibrant ecosystem. Who Should Attend? This session is ideal for: Entrepreneurs looking to understand greater Houston’s resources. Investors curious about the local startup landscape. Professionals and students wanting to connect with the innovation community. Anyone passionate about Houston’s growth as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship. Innovators who have recently moved to greater Houston and are looking to get “plugged in” to the local scene. Community leaders and service providers that support (or want to support) the innovation ecosystem. Register today for this chance to explore Houston’s ecosystem, uncover its flow, and help shape its future.

item.title: Fourth Saturday Phenology Walk
item.description:
Saturday, August 22, 2026 at 9 AM

Fourth Saturday of the Month9:00 – 11:00 amFree, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Meet in front of the Nature Center building Discover the hidden seasonal rhythms of nature firsthand on our guided Phenology Walks, where we track the life cycles of different plants across ecosystems, from the first spring bud burst to winter dormancy. You’ll learn how shifting weather patterns and climate change influence the timing of these important events in our local ecosystems and how you can become a community scientist, contributing vital data from your own backyard to a global research initiative. These relaxing morning walks are led by scientists from Rice University and staff from the Arboretum. We welcome nature enthusiasts of all ages, however kids 12 years and younger must be accompanied by a guardian. Learn more about the study of phenology and ways you can contribute at https://www.usanpn.org/nn Community Science Partner

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Inprint Andrea Bajani & Claire Vaye Watkins Reading
item.description:
Monday, August 24, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Congregation Emanu El, 1500 Sunset Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

Season tickets are on sale here.   Andrea Bajani and Claire Vaye Watkins will read from their new novels The Anniversary (translated by Geoffrey Brock) and Yellow Pine, respectively, followed by an on-stage conversation led by professor and National Book Critics Circle Award finalist Lacy M. Johnson. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Andrea Bajani is one of the most recognized and lauded authors of contemporary Italian and European literature. His many novels include If You Kept a Record of Sins, called “astonishing” by The New York Times, and Every Promise, which won the Bagutta Prize, the oldest Italian literary prize. A self-described existential writer, he often examines the personal, philosophical, and political, while confronting the unanswerable. A professor and international writer-in-residence at Rice University, Bajani joins us with his latest novel, The Anniversary, which won the 2025 Strega Prize, one of Europe’s major literary awards. Currently being translated into more than 25 languages, The Anniversary is a subtle yet heartrending portrait of an abusive marriage in patriarchal Italy and a son’s liberating decision to cut contact with his parents. The Times Literary Supplement writes, “Bajani’s prose is sharp and brims with psychological insights . . . Perhaps its most salient feature—in deft translation by Geoffrey Brock—is its skill at depicting alienation . . . Like Albert Camus, Bajani is a poet of estrangement.” Claire Vaye Watkins has been called “the most riveting voice of the unsalvageable West” (Los Angeles Times). Her debut novel Gold Fame Citrus, inspired by the Californian drought and by the lives of outcasts in the desert, blends climate fiction with environmental history. Born in Bishop, California and raised in the Mojave Desert on the Amargosa River, Watkins is also the author of the novel I Love You But I’ve Chosen Darkness and the short story collection Battleborn, winner of the Story Prize, the Dylan Thomas Prize, and the New York Public Library’s Young Lions Fiction Award. A National Book Foundation “5 Under 35” honoree and a Guggenheim Fellow, Watkins comes to Houston with her newest work Yellow Pine, described by author Megha Majumdar as “an exhilarating novel about a woman in the Mojave desert who wants to be a mother one more time, wants to love freely and arrange her life freely, wants to live outside the maze of money and ads and being sold to, a novel with huge and electric convictions.” Lacy M. Johnson is a Houston-based professor, curator, and activist, and is author of The Reckonings and The Other Side — both National Book Critics Circle Award finalists — and Trespasses. She is editor, with the designer Cheryl Beckett, of More City Than Water: A Houston Flood Atlas. She teaches creative nonfiction at Rice University, where she is the Director of the MFA in Creative Writing Program, and is also the Founding Director of the Houston Flood Museum.

From Inprint Houston

item.description:

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Urbanism Continuum CE day   9:00-9:30am Breakfast and Registration 9:30-10:45am / Presentation Building Bridges: Collaborative Placemaking in the Bayou City – 1.25 AIA HSW Presented by Michael Robinson, PLA, ASLA, Principal, SWA Group Michael is a landscape architect focused on the intersection of infrastructure and public space. He leads the design and implementation of complex park, trail, and civic landscape projects, connecting regional systems into cohesive, accessible environments. His work spans planning through realization, coordinating multidisciplinary teams and public agencies to deliver resilient, buildable solutions. With a background in both architecture and landscape architecture, he brings a systems-based approach that integrates environmental performance, mobility, and user experience into high-performing public landscapes. 11:00-12:00pm / Presentation  Universal Design: Building Accessible and Healthy Spaces – 1.00 AIA HSW (Barrier Free) Presented by Kyle J. Mutz, Director, University of Houston / Justin Dart Jr. Student Accessibility Center Kyle is the Director of the Justin Dart Jr. Student Accessibility Center at the University of Houston, where he champions accessibility, inclusion, and student success. Drawing from both his professional expertise and lived experience growing up with a disability, Kyle is committed to creating equitable opportunities for all. A former U.S. wheelchair racing athlete, he brings a unique perspective on disability advocacy and is dedicated to advancing the legacy of Justin Dart Jr. through education and empowerment.   12:00-12:30pm – Break for Lunch    12:30-1:45pm / Presentation  From Paint to Policy: How Tactical Urbanism Became a Capital Project – 1.25 AIA HSW & 1.25 LA/CES HSW Presented by Ed Pettitt, MPH – President of Columbia Tap and Urban Planner with Asakura Robinson Ed is an urban planner and One Health specialist whose academic path spans human biology at Cornell University, global health and healthcare management at the University of Texas School of Public Health, and doctoral studies in Urban Planning and Environmental Policy at Texas Southern University. In addition, Ed is also the President of the Columbia Tap Trail.  He provides organizational leadership by guiding the board, strengthening partnerships, advancing strategic initiatives, and overseeing programs that support equitable community development along the Columbia Tap Trail. 2:00-3:15pm / Presentation + Tour Reclaiming Main Street: Designing a Lasting Legacy in the Public Realm  – 1.25 AIA HSW & 1.25 LA/CES HSW Presented by Alex Ramirez, PLA & Sarah Smith, PLA, CDT, Design Workshop Alex is a Principal in the Houston studio at Design Workshop, with expertise as both a landscape architect and urban designer. His diverse experience spans across the private and public sectors, involving every phase of the design process—from conceptual planning and site analysis to construction documentation and detailed observation. Alex is dedicated to delivering top-tier work by crafting innovative design solutions for plazas, streetscapes, parks, and open spaces. His approach integrates social, cultural, economic, and environmental considerations, ensuring that each project enhances the surrounding neighborhoods and communities in meaningful ways. Sarah is a landscape architect in our Houston studio with a passion for the outdoors, thoughtful design, and creating meaningful places. From concept through construction, she brings creativity, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to projects ranging from parks and corporate campuses to urban streetscapes. Sarah earned her Bachelor of Landscape Architecture from Louisiana State University and is an active member of ULI, Central Houston, and ASLA.   Continuing Education Credits: AIA = 4.75 HSW LA/CES = 3.75 HSW   Individual classes are not available for the event. item.title: EnLAce: Domino Night with LiA Maestros
item.description:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

This year’s Enlace introduces a new and engaging format: a rotating domino game night designed to spark genuine conversations and connections in a relaxed, interactive environment. Through time-based gameplay and table rotations, participants will have the opportunity to engage with several LiA Maestros throughout the evening, creating a unique, fun, and memorable mentoring experience. EnLAce is open to all professionals looking for career development and growth. No dominoes experience required. We will begin the evening with a brief tutorial to make it easy and enjoyable for everyone to participate. Luis Ayala, AIA, Luis Ayala Studio Sofia Fonseca de Nino, AIA Michael Gonzales, AIA, protolab Yvette Herrera Duran, Assoc. AIA, Stantec Daniel Ortiz, AIA, RDLR Bayardo Selva, AIA, Cre8 Cindy Villareal, AIA, O’Connell Robertson Luis Ayala, AIA, Owner, Luis Ayala Studio Luis is a Paraguayan architect that migrated to Houston in 2007. He has focused mostly on the design of education facilities for higher education institutions and K-12 schools. His expertise includes campus design, master planning, programming, and facility design. Luis has many other skills that complement his abilities as a designer and architect. Sustainability is one of Luis’s stronger interests, and many of his projects have received design awards recognizing his innovation in green design. Luis is also an avid architectural photographer, recognized in 2017 by the Texas Society of Architects with the Award for Excellence in the Promotion of Architecture Trough the Media. Luis fluently speaks Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, and English. In 2016, Luis was distinguished by YAF Houston as a part Emerging Voices Exhibition and later the same year by AIA National as an Emerging Professional. Recently, in 2020 the AIA Houston awarded him with the Ben Brewer Award for Young Architects. Michael Gonzales, AIA, Owner, protolab Michael Gonzales is the owner and principal of Protolab Architects. Michael specializes in digital fabrication innovation for civic, cultural and commercial projects. He has extensive experience working with the latest fabrication technologies to develop efficient strategies for optimal construction and project delivery at all scales and complexities. Michael is also an Instructional Associate Professor at the University of Houston Gerald D. Hines College of Architecture and Design where he focuses on the integration of digital design and fabrication. He actively publishes and lectures on emerging techniques in computation and design Yvette Herrera Duran, Assoc. AIA, Stantec Yvette Herrera Duran is an architectural designer based in Houston Texas. Her experience expands from many years in high-end residential design to now corporate commercial architecture at Page. Born and raised in Guatemala, she moved to Miami to pursue her Undergraduate Studies in Interior Design at Florida International University. After working for a few years at a high-end residential architecture firm, where architecture and interiors were strongly interconnected, she pursued her master’s in architecture at Rice University. From an early age she was trained in flamenco dancing, which she has continued practicing. During her years in Miami, she trained in ballroom dance and later, while getting her masters, she complimented her knowledge in the arts with theatre classes.  All these various art languages influence how she experiences spaces and the development of her detailed oriented designs.  She currently works in various design typologies from academic to healthcare to multifamily communities. Bayardo Selva, AIA, Cre8 Bayardo has turn his childhood building blocks play time into an Architectural career that expands over 20 years. His experienced has allowed him to engage a wide variety of project types and scales. He actively participates in the community through different organizations promoting architecture, protecting the environment, mentoring the youth and celebrating diversity including AIA Houston Young Architects Forum (Chair, 2014), AIA Board of Directors 2015-2018 and 2023-present (AIAH Board President, 2026), Houston Hispanic Architects and Engineers Board Member 2016-2019, Houston MOD Board Member 2019-Present, Houston Fit Running Club 2012-Present, and founding member of the AIA Houston Latinos in Architecture. He considers himself a student of the profession and enjoys perfecting his craft! Cindy Villareal, AIA, Houston Office Director, O’Connell Robertson Cindy Villarreal is a seasoned leader in architectural planning and project acquisition, with a strong focus on higher education and healthcare initiatives across Texas. As the Houston Office Director, Cindy is instrumental in expanding business development efforts throughout the Houston region while driving strategic growth statewide. With decades of experience in the design of higher education and Science and Technology facilities, Cindy has led projects ranging from allied health and nursing schools to dental institutions and advanced diagnostics and neuroscience laboratories. Her expertise lies in managing multidisciplinary design teams and fostering collaboration to ensure projects are delivered successfully. Cindy is a passionate advocate for sustainable and resilient design. She champions human-centric environments that prioritize occupant well-being and support thriving communities. Her leadership continues to shape spaces that are not only functional and efficient but also inspiring and inclusive.

From AIA Houston

item.description:
Wednesday, August 26, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Houston Maritime Center & Museum, 2940 Riverby Rd, Suite 200, Houston, TX, 77020, United States

Offshore Wind Drinks – Houston Hosted By National Wildlife Federation – Free event. Please sign up to attend For nearly twenty years, Texas has led the nation in producing wind power. Texas now hosts nearly 20,000 active wind turbines—more than the next three states (Iowa, Oklahoma, and California) combined! Offshore Wind presents a remarkable opportunity for Texas to continue its role as a maritime industry and energy leader. Enthusiastic support and advanced planning will ensure that Texas is ready to advance responsible offshore wind development in the years to come. The National Wildlife Federation invites you to join us for Offshore Wind Drinks on Wednesday, August 26th, at 6 pm CDT, at the Houston Maritime Center and Museum. This event will feature guest speaker Janet Harreld, the Executive Director of the Office of Continuing Education at the University of Houston-Downtown (UHD). Join us to learn more about UHD’s Wind Turbine Technician Program and the ways that Texas is already contributing to the development of offshore wind energy on the East Coast. Come mix and mingle while learning about this emerging, reliable energy option that is producing power and creating high-quality jobs. We hope you’ll join us! item.description:

Location: Houston Heights City Hall & Fire Station, 107 W. 12th Street, Houston, TX, 77008, United States

AUGUST 26th at 6:30pm, join us at the Heights Fire Station Carolyn, of Angel Wing Arts, (Instagram @cacoatesart or @anglewingarts) and one of our own, will lead this workshop. Carolyn has been active in the arts for over 30 years, from faux finishes to murals to art pieces. She has worked with clients and their art needs, and her work itself is whimsical and fun. Please join us on August 26, at our favorite spot to mingle, the historic Heights Fire station on 12th and Yale streets. There will be a demo, and plenty of inspiration to kick off your creativity!! Let’s help our bees and butterflies in this heat by providing them a safe place to get a drink that YOU are providing with your cute, personalized vessel. item.title: Author Talk with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon From Chicago
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Albert and Ethel Herzstein Theater on the Mady and Ken Kades Stage

Join Holocaust Museum Houston for a night with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon from Chicago: The Untold Story of an American Reporter in Nazi Germany.      “Today we face an alarming upsurge in the spread of misinformation and attempts by powerful figures to discredit facts so they can seize control of our political and cultural narratives. These are threats American journalist Sigrid Schultz knew all too well. The Chicago Tribune’s Berlin bureau chief and primary foreign correspondent for Central Europe from 1925 to January 1941, Schultz witnessed Hitler’s rise to power and was one of the first reporters—male or female—to warn American readers of the growing dangers of Nazism.  She was one of the last to leave Berlin before it was too late.     In The Dragon From Chicago, historian Pamela Toler tells the story of Schultz’s years spent courageously reporting the news from Berlin, from the revolts of 1919 through the Nazi rise to power and Allied air raids over Berlin in 1941. At a time when women reporters rarely wrote front-page stories, Schultz regularly  reported the truth about Nazi Germany in the face of censorship and the threat of expulsion, internment, or death. The Nazis called Schultz “that dragon from Chicago.” One of her fellow correspondents called her “Adolph Hitler’s greatest enemy.” Schultz herself claimed to be “just a reporter.” Her story is a powerful account of one woman standing up for truth in an era marked by the spread of disinformation and propaganda spawned by hate.”     Books will be available for purchase by credit card.

From Holocaust Museum Houston

item.title: National Beyblade League
item.description:
Sunday, August 30, 2026 at 10 AM

🌀 National Beyblade League: Beyblade X CCS Tournament 🌀 Bladers, it’s time to step into the stadium. The National Beyblade League is teaming up with CCS Houston for a full day dedicated to Beyblade X. Battle through the tournament, challenge new rivals in free play, meet fellow bladers, and spend the day celebrating one of the fastest-growing competitive hobbies.   📅 Sunday, August 30 | 10AM–5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   ⚡ Event Highlights ⚡   🏆 National Beyblade League x CCS Tournament | 12PM – 5PM Bring your strongest combos into the stadium and compete in the official National Beyblade League x CCS Tournament. Tournament Features: The tournament begins with a 64-player group stage, where bladers battle to earn a spot in the Top 16. Once the field is set, the competition shifts to a single-elimination bracket, where every match brings you one step closer to the championship. Prize packages for top finishers: More info on prizes coming soon 👉 Sign-ups here: https://nbl.challonge.com/NBLCCS Think you’ve built the ultimate combo? It’s time to prove it in the stadium.   🏟️ Beyblade X Free Play Arena The battles don’t stop when the brackets do. Jump into the Free Play Arena to test new combos, run casual matches, practice launches, and challenge other bladers outside of tournament rounds.   🎮 More Than Just Beyblade Explore even more collectibles throughout the show floor with CCS vendors featuring trading cards, anime collectibles, retro games, toys, figures, and more. The stadium is ready. The brackets are set. The only thing missing is your launch. Join the National Beyblade League: Beyblade X CCS Tournament and see what your combo can do. 🌀 LET IT RIP! 🌀

From CCS Houston

Celebrate Rosh Hashanah with a joyful “Happy Birthday to the World” celebration! This special family event is presented in partnership with the Evelyn Rubenstein JCC, PJ Library and the Jewish Federation of Greater Houston. Join us on the last Sunday in August as we welcome the Jewish New Year. In Jewish tradition, Rosh Hashanah is known as Yom Harat Olam, the birthday of the world. Bring the whole family for an afternoon filled with festive fun, meaningful traditions and hands-on activities that celebrate the sweetness of the New Year. Children and families will enjoy music, inflatables, games, crafts, story time, a photo booth and much more! item.description:
Friday, September 4, 2026 at 3 PM

Houston TCG Con XI – The Long Weekend Belongs to Your Binder Labor Day weekend is three days off. Spend at least part of it doing what you actually love. Houston TCG Con XI runs Friday night through Sunday afternoon – Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, MTG, One Piece, Lorcana, Riftbound, and more across a curated vendor floor where the person across the table is already looking for what you’ve got.   📅 Friday, September 4 to Sunday, September 6, 2026 ⏰ Friday 3PM – 10PM | Saturday 10AM – 5PM | Sunday 10AM – 5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St, Unit 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 🃏 Every Major TCG on One Curated Houston Floor Pokémon, Yu-Gi-Oh!, MTG, One Piece, Lorcana, Riftbound, Dragon Ball Super, Digimon, Flesh and Blood, and more. Find singles, sealed product, graded slabs, Japanese imports, vintage favorites, and competitive staples all in one place.   🤝 Buy • Sell • Trade — All Weekend This is a buy-sell-trade floor, not a one-way shopping trip. The vendors here are collectors first.   🔍 On-Site Grading Submissions & Card Restorations — Cappy’s Cards! Have a card you’ve been thinking about grading? Or one that needs a little restoration? Cappy’s Cards will be on-site helping collectors with grading submissions, restoration services, and expert insight all weekend.   💼 Interested in Vending? If you’ve got singles, sealed product, graded slabs, TCG accessories, or anything else the Houston community is hunting this Labor Day weekend, apply here → https://tinyurl.com/HoustonTCGCon   🏨 Staying the Weekend? Three days is worth the trip. Book your stay: Here The last long weekend of summer is yours. Houston TCG Con XI.

item.description:
Saturday, September 5, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: The Commons

Join us for a peaceful morning experience in Hermann Park with a free guided Sound Bath led by Daemein Smith of Prioritizing Peace. Set against the natural beauty of the Tsuru Family Terrace in the Commons, this immersive meditation experience uses sound and vibration to promote relaxation, mindfulness, and emotional well-being. Guests are encouraged to slow down, reset, and “Prioritize Peace” through a calming journey of sound healing in nature.  Tsuru Family Terrace Saturday, September 5  8 – 9 a.m.  Free Community Session Guests are encouraged to bring a yoga mat if available. Blankets and pillows are also recommended for additional comfort. All ages and experience levels welcome. Parking: Free parking available across the street from the Commons in Lot S (6215 Main St, Houston, TX 77030). Additional street parking available along Main Street.

item.title: Edible Wild Plants
item.description:
Sunday, September 6, 2026 at 1 PM

$100 member / $125 nonmember (per person)Ages 16+, minors must be accompanied by an adult For most of human existence, the wilds supplied all our food and medicine. Join Dr. Mark “Merriwether” Vorderbruggen as he teaches you what your ancestors knew. This plant walkabout will give you hands-on (as well as nose, fingers, and taste bud) guidance on how to properly identify and utilize the wonderful wild plants of the Houston/East Texas region. Please dress for the weather and wear walking shoes. register online Instructor bio: Dr. Mark Vorderbruggen brings his background as a Ph.D. in chemistry to the world of Houston’s edible and medicinal wild plants. He is the author of “The Idiot’s Guide: Foraging,” runs the informative “Foraging Texas” website, formulates medicinal plant remedies through Medicine Man Plant Co., and is always educating about useful plants on TV, online, and in person.

item.title: Discover Nature Together Scavenger Hunts
item.description:
Sunday, September 6, 2026 at 2 PM

Free, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Bring the whole family to the Houston Arboretum for free, themed scavenger hunts! Each month features a themed self-guided scavenger hunt where families can join us at our Nature Center before heading out to the trails to sharpen their observation skills and learn something new about nature. From spiders to fall foliage, every adventure is different! Please come prepared for the outdoors (closed toe shoes recommended, bring a water bottle, bug spray, etc).  Signs of LifeSeptember 6 We may not always see animals out and about, so how do we know they are here? They leave traces of themselves behind! From scat, to tracks, learn how to find the signs of life here at the Arboretum. Amazing ArachnidsOctober 10 Spiders are so much more than Halloween decorations. They fill the role of pest control specialist in our ecosystem. Want to learn more about these amazing arachnids? Then get into the Halloween spirit by learning more about spiders. Fall FoliageNovember 7 Although Houston is not known for its fall colors, there are still lots to learn about leaves! From deciduous to evergreen, here at the Arboretum we see leaves on the ground as well as in the trees all winter long. Join us and learn more about the difference between the two and why leaves are important in the fall. Animal HomesDecember 5 There is no central heating outdoors, so where do the animals go when they get cold? To their homes, of course! Burrows, leaves, nests, and so much more. Find out all the different types of animal homes and who lives in what.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Hatchlings
item.description:
Wednesday, September 9, 2026 at 10 AM

For children 0 – 18 months and their caregivers Babies in nature? Babies ARE nature! Babies who spend time outside are stronger, healthier, more confident, and better sleepers. Learn how to support your Hatchlings as they develop motor skills, test physical limits, cultivate their sense of wonder, and get messy in a safe place to try new things. Hatchlings will engage in outdoor nature play in this unique opportunity to interact, explore, and bond with their caregivers in the natural world. This program will be held outdoors and will include loose parts and messy play with natural sensory elements such as sand, mud, grass, sticks, leaves, and water. Space is limited and pre-registration is required for all Hatchlings classes. Select Wednesdays from 10:00 am – 11:00 am. Arboretum Member registration for Fall 2026 classes opens Tuesday, August 4 and Nonmember registration opens Tuesday, August 11. Become a Family Tree Member or above to access early registration and receive the Member rate. Pricing $12 member / $15 nonmember Per child/caregiver pair, per classMore than one caregiver may accompany a registered child. Minors must be accompanied by an adult. Upcoming Classes September september 9 september 16 september 23 November november 4 november 11 november 18 Additional Information Hatchlings classes are best for infants and toddlers who are creepers, crawlers, or new walkers up to 18 months old (not for older siblings), but even newborns benefit from sensory outdoor experiences Hatchlings will be held outdoors in rain or shine. Please dress yourself and your Hatchling for the weather and bring a spare change of clothes for your Hatchling. Hatchlings classes are for children 0-18 months and their caregivers only. Please do not bring older siblings to class. Accessibility This program is open to all abilities. Some areas where classes might be held are not stroller-friendly or wheelchair accessible. Please plan to carry your Hatchling to various locations and let us know if you need assistance with caregiver accessibility.

item.description:
