Location: McGovern Centennial Gardens, 1500 Hermann Drive, Houston, TX, 77004, United States

Join Hermann Park Conservancy on Friday, September 11, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. for a meaningful morning of service in Hermann Park. In recognition of the 9/11 National Day of Service and Remembrance, volunteers will unite for good by participating in hands-on projects that help care for and beautify the Park. Date & Time:Friday, September 11, 20261 – 3:30 PM Location:The Lighthouse of Houston3602 West Dallas St, Houston, TX 77019 Event Description:Join us for the inaugural Lighthouse Open House 2026, a dynamic and inclusive event designed for people who are blind, have low vision, or live with a disability. Event Highlights:Employment Resume-building workshops and interview prep Meet-and-greet with inclusive employers Tips for navigating the workplace with vision loss Technology Hands-on demonstrations of assistive technology and low vision devices Tutorials on screen readers, magnifiers, and accessible apps Try-before-you-buy opportunities with top vendors Health & Community Resources Free health screenings (blood pressure, glucose, and more) Behavioral health and wellness sessions Diabetes education and vision-specific health tips Information on transportation, housing, and benefits assistance Access to local nonprofits, support organizations, and accessible recreation Whether you’re seeking tools for independence, looking to connect with community services, or exploring inclusive employment, this expo is for you. Please Note: Registration begins August 11. Check back soon!

item.description:
Friday, September 11, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: The Lighthouse of Houston, 3602 West Dallas, Houston, TX, 77019, United States

Turn the volume up and the worries down—SINGO Bingo is back, and it’s here to play louder than ordinary bingo ever could. This monthly favorite blends the joy of music with the thrill of the game. Songs replace numbers, laughter replaces silence, and every round becomes a shared rhythm of anticipation. Designed with accessibility at the center, SINGO Bingo features Braille and large-print cards so participants who are blind or low vision can play fully, confidently, and independently. Free and open to the community, this is a night to unwind, connect, and let the music carry you. No pressure. No experience required. Just good company, great sound, and a little luck along the way. item.title: Inprint Cool Brains! Series presents Rex Ogle
item.description:
Sunday, September 13, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: Meyerland Performing and Visual Arts Middle School, 10410 Manhattan Drive, Houston, TX, 77096, United States

Free and open to the public Free copies of one of Rex Ogle’s newest books for the first 100 families Presentation and Q&A by the author Meet the author followed by a book sale and signing Bus scholarships available for student groups – full scholarships for public schools, partial scholarships for private schools upon availability. For information, email info@inprint.org Discounted books available through Brazos Bookstore And more! The 2026/2027 Inprint Cool Brains! Series proudly presents award-winning author Rex Ogle, sharing his new books Fruitcake, a graphic novel about surviving middle school and finding the courage to be yourself, and Absent, a middle grade novel about three boys who skip school, told in verse, prose, and comics. Rex Ogle is the author of more than 100 books for kids, including comics, graphic novels, and memoirs—most notably Free Lunch (winner of the ALA/YALSA award for Excellence in Nonfiction), Abuela Don’t Forget Me (ALA/YALSA award for Excellence in Nonfiction finalist), Road Home (a Micheal Printz Honor and Stonewall Honor book), and middle grade graphic novels Four Eyes and Pizza Face. Under his pseudonym Rey Terciero, he has also reimagined classics as modern and diverse graphic novels, including Meg, Jo, Beth, & Amy, Northranger (nominated for both Harvey and GLAAD Media Awards), and Dan in Green Gables (nominated for a GLAAD Media Award). Born and raised in Texas, Rex now lives in Los Angeles where he writes every day—when he’s not reading X-Men, gaming with friends, or chasing his dog, Toby, trying to score a hug. Described as “funny, sad, goofy and poignant; a winner” (Kirkus starred review), Fruitcake is the third and final installment of Ogle’s highly popular Four Eyes graphic novel series, which tackles relatable middle school themes like bullying, puberty, building self-confidence, and navigating friendships. Eighth grade isn’t off to a great start for Rex. Everyone seems to be coupling up, and he’s starting to feel like an outsider—until he meets Charlotte. She’s fearless, smart, pretty, and, best of all, she likes him back. But as wonderful as Charlotte is, Rex can’t stop thinking about someone else: Drew, Rex’s childhood best friend. Suddenly, Rex is navigating feelings he never expected. With strong opinions swirling at home and church, Rex begins to question his own worth and what his feelings truly mean. Featuring Dave Valeza’s vibrant, colorful, and engaging illustrations, Fruitcake is a heartfelt story of laughter and fear, crushes and coming out, and the courage it takes to embrace who you are. With illustrations by LJ-Baptiste, Absent explores school absenteeism in a compelling, entertaining, and utterly distinct middle grade novel. With a dad in jail and a lack of teachers interested in helping him learn, Manny doesn’t see the point in anything besides skateboarding and writing lyrics. Calvin has so many responsibilities to his father and little brothers that when his bike is stolen, he can’t make it to school on time. And while Liam is studious and wants to become a doctor, he is tormented by bullies and hides out in an unused janitor’s closet instead of going to class. When the boys are thrown together in detention, they realize that they might still have a lot to learn—not just from their teachers, but from each other. Absent tells the boys’ stories in three distinct voices: Manny’s in verse, Calvin’s as a comic, and Liam’s as a prose journal. ***Please note that the book signing will be conducted on a first-come, first-served basis. Upon entering the theater, people wishing to have books signed will be given a number, and the book signing will take place in numerical order after the on-stage presentation.***

From Inprint Houston

Wilson Realty Co. began developing Woodland Heights in 1907 on 136 acres of land that was once part of John Austin's Mexican land grant. item.title: Inprint Claudia Rankine Reading
item.description:
Monday, September 14, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Brockman Hall for Opera, Rice University, Entrance #18 off Rice Boulevard, Houston, TX, 77005

General admission tickets will go on sale on Tuesday, August 25, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Claudia Rankine will read from her new hybrid-genre work Triage, followed by an on-stage conversation led by poet and Rice University professor Phillip B. Williams. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Whether writing about intimacy or alienation, Claudia Rankine possesses a voice of unrelenting candor that “shimmers with wisdom and fury” (The Telegraph). A MacArthur Fellow, Rankine is the author of five collections of poetry, including her bestselling Citizen: An American Lyric, which explores what it means to be an American citizen in a “post-racial” society. A defining text for our time, Citizen won the National Book Critics Circle Award, the NAACP Image Award, the PEN Open Book Award, and the Los Angeles Times Book Prize. She is also the author of three plays, including Provenance of Beauty: A South Bronx Travelogue, which is performed on a bus ride through the Bronx; and is the editor of several anthologies, including The Racial Imaginary: Writers on Race in the Life of the Mind. Rankine returns to Inprint with her genre-defying new work Triage, which collides the lyric with narrative, memoir, image, and essay to offer her most personal and emotionally resonant writing yet. Triage follows the turbulent friendship between two characters, the narrator and the theorist, self-identified sisters struggling to define their wounded histories and their shared but separate lives. According to Jamaica Kincaid, “Claudia Rankine’s remarkable, outstanding odyssey—an account of our present, which is also our past, which is always our future—is beautifully rendered in a kaleidoscope of images and sensations. . . . Triage is exquisite.”

From Inprint Houston

item.description:
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: Houston Food Bank East Branch, 535 Portwall Street, Houston, TX, 77029, United States

Did you know that on Tuesday, September 15th, it’s National Voter Registration Day! At Houston Food Bank, we care about having your voice heard, and we are proud to provide the opportunity for you to register to vote on National Voter Registration Day! We are partnering with Harris County Tax Office and the National Voter Registration Day organization to serve as a site for Voter Registration at our Portwall location. You are eligible to register to vote if: You are a United States citizen; You are a resident of the county where you submit the application; You are at least 17 years and 10 months old on the date your voter registration application is submitted, and you are 18 years of age on Election Day. You are not a convicted felon (you may be eligible to vote if you have completed your sentence, probation, and parole); and You have not been declared by a court exercising probate jurisdiction to be either totally mentally incapacitated or partially mentally incapacitated without the right to vote. item.title: Latinos in Architecture: MaS
item.description:
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Architecture Center Houston, 902 Commerce St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

The Latinos in Architecture (LiA) collegiate Mentorship and Scholarship program (MaS), through AIA Houston and Architecture Center Houston, intends to bridge the gap between students and professionals in the Latino architecture community. The MaS program matches college students pursuing a career path in architecture with a mentor who has an established career in the field. The program is for Latino students who are striving to influence the future of the built environment and the architecture profession. MaS will kick off on September 15, 2026, and conclude in May 2027. PROGRAM ELIGIBILITYfor the mentorship: Students have the option to participate only in the mentorship program and not pursue the scholarship. But students are welcome to participate in any MaS-related events. Students pursuing a degree in architecture at the University of Houston, Rice University, or Prairie View A&M University. The program is open to both US citizens and foreign students. for the scholarship: Students with at least one more academic year to apply scholarship funds directly to tuition.  Students with full scholarships are not eligible. SCHOLARSHIP REQUIREMENTSThe 2026-2027 program starts in September 2026 and ends in May 2027. Regularly check in with an assigned mentor (at least 4 times). These meetings can be in-person, virtual, or via phone call.  ​Participate in the kick-off event where they will meet the mentors. Kick-off will take place September 15 at 7pm.  Participate in the portfolio review organized by the LiA Committee. Attend three LiA, AIAH, TSA or HNOMA-sponsored events. Not including student chapters or student-led events. Attend their university or college career fair. Submit a PDF on a project or portfolio at the end of the Fall semester. Submit a 5-minute video on a project or portfolio at the end of the Spring semester. The video should not be a recording of a class crit and should not exceed 5 minutes. AWARDS Students must participate in the listed activities to be considered for the scholarship. These activities are meant to support and complement the student’s academic career. Scholarships will be awarded based on student participation in the program and their end-of-semester submission, which will be reviewed by a jury. 

From AIA Houston

item.title: Hatchlings
item.description:
Wednesday, September 16, 2026 at 10 AM

For children 0 – 18 months and their caregivers Babies in nature? Babies ARE nature! Babies who spend time outside are stronger, healthier, more confident, and better sleepers. Learn how to support your Hatchlings as they develop motor skills, test physical limits, cultivate their sense of wonder, and get messy in a safe place to try new things. Hatchlings will engage in outdoor nature play in this unique opportunity to interact, explore, and bond with their caregivers in the natural world. This program will be held outdoors and will include loose parts and messy play with natural sensory elements such as sand, mud, grass, sticks, leaves, and water. Space is limited and pre-registration is required for all Hatchlings classes. Select Wednesdays from 10:00 am – 11:00 am. Arboretum Member registration for Fall 2026 classes opens Tuesday, August 4 and Nonmember registration opens Tuesday, August 11. Become a Family Tree Member or above to access early registration and receive the Member rate. Pricing $12 member / $15 nonmember Per child/caregiver pair, per classMore than one caregiver may accompany a registered child. Minors must be accompanied by an adult. Upcoming Classes September september 9 september 16 september 23 November november 4 november 11 november 18 Additional Information Hatchlings classes are best for infants and toddlers who are creepers, crawlers, or new walkers up to 18 months old (not for older siblings), but even newborns benefit from sensory outdoor experiences Hatchlings will be held outdoors in rain or shine. Please dress yourself and your Hatchling for the weather and bring a spare change of clothes for your Hatchling. Hatchlings classes are for children 0-18 months and their caregivers only. Please do not bring older siblings to class. Accessibility This program is open to all abilities. Some areas where classes might be held are not stroller-friendly or wheelchair accessible. Please plan to carry your Hatchling to various locations and let us know if you need assistance with caregiver accessibility.

item.title: Unified Topgolf Pro-Am (Houston-Katy)
item.description:
Friday, September 18, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Topgolf-Katy, 1030 Memorial Brook Blvd, Houston, TX 77084, Houston, 77084

The Unified Topgolf Pro-Am is one of the most exciting and meaningful community partnership events hosted by Special Olympics Texas, bringing together athletes, families, coaches, volunteers, corporate partners, and local business leaders for an unforgettable day of golf, laughter, connection, and community impact. Each bay includes a Special Olympics Texas athlete paired alongside five golfers, creating a truly unique experience where relationships, memories, and meaningful moments are built throughout the day. From friendly competition and team spirit to incredible conversations and shared experiences, the event is designed to bring people together in a fun and welcoming environment while directly supporting local athletes and programs. Proceeds from the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am help provide year-round sports training, competitions, health initiatives, leadership development, and educational opportunities for children, teenagers, and adults with intellectual disabilities throughout the greater Houston area. As the event continues growing each year, the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am has quickly become a tremendous opportunity for organizations and community members to make a real impact while being part of something incredibly energetic, uplifting, and memorable. For more information regarding sponsorship opportunities, team entries, volunteer involvement, or sponsorship opportunities, please reach out to Jared Kossover, Strategic Partnerships Manager with Special Olympics Texas Jared Kossover E: jkossover@sotx.org C: 737-867-9659

item.title: The Brookwood Way Conference Sept 22-24
item.description:
Monday, September 21, 2026 at 9 AM

Location: The Brookwood Community Main Campus, 1752 FM 1489, Brookshire, TX, 77423, United States

Experience The Brookwood Way – A Conference That Changes Everything September 21–25, 2026 from 8:30am–4:00pm at The Brookwood Community, Brookshire, Texas This three-day conference provides an engaging, behind-the-scenes experience designed to fully immerse participants in our culture, methodology, and practices, which we call The Brookwood Way. Discover a proven, purpose-driven model that empowers adults with disabilities to live with dignity, purpose, and meaningful work. The Brookwood Way Conference is an immersive, behind-the-scenes experience at The Brookwood Community in Brookshire, Texas, created for leaders, families, nonprofits, ministries, and organizations seeking to build or strengthen thriving communities for adults with disabilities. Experience The Brookwood Way firsthand as you tour our campus, connect with our leadership team, and see a living model in action. You’ll leave inspired and equipped with practical ideas, proven strategies, and adaptable tools to help create communities where adults with disabilities can flourish. Who should attend? Individuals and organizations that are serving or desire to serve adults with disabilities Professionals who desire to create more opportunities for people with disabilities or other underserved populations Teachers, administrators, parents, church groups, healthcare professionals, non-profits or anyone seeking inspiration to make a difference $495 Early Bird Pricing (Conference Fee after Sept. 1—$550 per person) REGISTER TODAY What If Three Days Isn’t Enough? There are two PRE-Conference sessions and two POST-Conference sessions available! Choose a PRE-Conference Experience for Monday, Sept. 21: Satellite Immersion Opportunity – Get Inspired. See it in action! REGISTER HEREA unique pre-conference site visit to one of our Satellite Work Programs designed to provide a real-world glimpse into what a Brookwood-inspired start-up can look like. Both locations are generously donated spaces, reflecting our commitment to fiscal stewardship, and each visit includes a guided tour, time observing our Citizens at work, and lunch with a Brookwood leader who will share insights on startup strategy and building a mission-led program. OR Introduction to Handbells Workshop – Add music to your conference! REGISTER HERE Learn the basics of teaching handbells using a Brookwood-developed method, including proper technique for ringing handbells and handchimes and an introduction to reading adaptive notation. Helps you discover if this is an experience you would like to offer to those you serve. Choose a POST-Conference Experience for Friday, Sept. 25: Fundraising Essentials Course – Go Behind the Scenes with Brookwood’s Development Team! REGISTER HERELearn proven fundraising strategies from Brookwood’s Development Team, covering donor cultivation, foundation relationships, peer-to-peer fundraising, events, volunteer engagement, and donor management systems. OR Fundamentals of Citizen Life – Go Beyond the Tour and See how We Create Community REGISTER HERE An in-depth look at the divisions that make up Citizen Life at Brookwood: Residential, Work Program, Spiritual Life, Admissions, Medical, and Activities. Led by our department leaders, with time for Q&A.   Thank you for supporting the beloved adults with disABILITIES who live and work at Brookwood! Changing the way the world thinks about adults with disabilities Visit our Events Calendar for the full schedule of Brookwood’s upcoming events.  

From Nutcracker Market

item.title: Hatchlings
item.description:
Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 10 AM

For children 0 – 18 months and their caregivers Babies in nature? Babies ARE nature! Babies who spend time outside are stronger, healthier, more confident, and better sleepers. Learn how to support your Hatchlings as they develop motor skills, test physical limits, cultivate their sense of wonder, and get messy in a safe place to try new things. Hatchlings will engage in outdoor nature play in this unique opportunity to interact, explore, and bond with their caregivers in the natural world. This program will be held outdoors and will include loose parts and messy play with natural sensory elements such as sand, mud, grass, sticks, leaves, and water. Space is limited and pre-registration is required for all Hatchlings classes. Select Wednesdays from 10:00 am – 11:00 am. Arboretum Member registration for Fall 2026 classes opens Tuesday, August 4 and Nonmember registration opens Tuesday, August 11. Become a Family Tree Member or above to access early registration and receive the Member rate. Pricing $12 member / $15 nonmember Per child/caregiver pair, per classMore than one caregiver may accompany a registered child. Minors must be accompanied by an adult. Upcoming Classes September september 9 september 16 september 23 November november 4 november 11 november 18 Additional Information Hatchlings classes are best for infants and toddlers who are creepers, crawlers, or new walkers up to 18 months old (not for older siblings), but even newborns benefit from sensory outdoor experiences Hatchlings will be held outdoors in rain or shine. Please dress yourself and your Hatchling for the weather and bring a spare change of clothes for your Hatchling. Hatchlings classes are for children 0-18 months and their caregivers only. Please do not bring older siblings to class. Accessibility This program is open to all abilities. Some areas where classes might be held are not stroller-friendly or wheelchair accessible. Please plan to carry your Hatchling to various locations and let us know if you need assistance with caregiver accessibility.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.description:
Wednesday, September 23, 2026 at 12 PM

Location: The Lighthouse of Houston, 3602 West Dallas, Houston, TX, 77019, United States

The Lighthouse will be hosting a weekly Braille Club to help people learn functional Braille skills in a friendly group setting. The club meets every Wednesday from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM. We will use fun games and activities to help everyone gain useful skills for daily life. Members will learn how to read playing cards for games, label items around their homes, and read signs and elevator buttons in public places. To join the club, participants need access to email and a notebook to keep their handout papers organized. Because the group learns new things every week, it is highly recommended to attend each session so you do not miss out on any important tips. REGISTER HERE.

item.title: The Architectural History of Houston Street Skating
item.description:
Saturday, September 26, 2026 at 9 AM

Location: Tranquility Park, 400 Rusk, Houston, Texas, 77002

Join lifelong skateboarder and architectural historian Ted Barrow on a walking tour of the highlights of Houston’s Modernist and Late-Modernist architecture through a skateboarder’s perspective. The tour will cover key plazas and buildings which became local, state-wide, and eventually global skateboarding destinations from the late 1980’s to today. About Ted Barrow Theodore (Ted) Barrow is an art historian, writer, curator, and lecturer whose work bridges academic scholarship and contemporary currents. Born in Bolinas, California, he holds a Ph.D. in art history from the Graduate Center, CUNY, where he explored the Florida paintings of Winslow Homer and John Singer Sargent through an ecocritical lens. Barrow has taught at Barnard College, Baruch College, City College of New York, and the University of San Francisco. Outside of art and academia, he is a distinctive voice in skateboarding culture, known for This Old Ledge, a video series that investigates the cultural and architectural significance of global skate spots.”   This program is in conjunction with The Kinetics of Urban Movement, on view at the Architecture Center Houston from June 18-September 26.   Exhibition Sponsors and Community Partners Kinetics of Urban Movement is funded in part by the City of Houston through Houston Arts Alliance Cherries Wheels Honey Skate Club Houston Parks and Recreation Department Houston Skate Academy Select Skate ECOSYSTEMS Southside Skatepark

From AIA Houston

Join us on Saturday, September 26, for National Public Lands Day, the nation’s largest single-day volunteer event for public lands! This is your chance to give back to Hermann Park, one of Houston’s most cherished green spaces. Whether you’re pulling invasive weeds, planting native grasses or helping with trail maintenance, your time and energy will directly support the health and beauty of the park for generations to come. item.title: Fourth Saturday Phenology Walk
item.description:
Saturday, September 26, 2026 at 9 AM

Fourth Saturday of the Month9:00 – 11:00 amFree, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Meet in front of the Nature Center building Discover the hidden seasonal rhythms of nature firsthand on our guided Phenology Walks, where we track the life cycles of different plants across ecosystems, from the first spring bud burst to winter dormancy. You’ll learn how shifting weather patterns and climate change influence the timing of these important events in our local ecosystems and how you can become a community scientist, contributing vital data from your own backyard to a global research initiative. These relaxing morning walks are led by scientists from Rice University and staff from the Arboretum. We welcome nature enthusiasts of all ages, however kids 12 years and younger must be accompanied by a guardian. Learn more about the study of phenology and ways you can contribute at https://www.usanpn.org/nn Community Science Partner

item.title: Tyke Hikes
item.description:
Monday, September 28, 2026 at 9:30 AM

For children 18 months – 4 years Encourage your child’s curiosity about nature and spend time with them exploring outdoors! Children with an adult companion can join a naturalist for a story reading, a simple nature or sensory development activity, and a stroller-friendly hike on the beautiful Arboretum trails. Arrive dressed in close-toed shoes and comfortable play clothes. Be prepared for the weather including hat, sunscreen, jackets, raincoat, or rain boots, as needed. Enjoy an interesting new nature experience each week with themes such as ponds, bones, senses, and leaves.  Select Mondays9:30 am-10:15 am10:30 am-11:15 am pricing Free for Family Tree Members and above (please have member card on hand)$7 per child for nonmembers, pay at the door. No preregistration is necessary; however, attendance is limited to 20 children per session. Sign-up will take place in front of the Beautyberry Classroom. Doors will close 15 minutes after the class begins or once the session is full. Siblings who are not within the age range may attend but may not participate. upcoming hikes September 14, 21, 28October 5, 12, 26November 2, 9, 16December 7, 14, 21 TYKE HIKES EN ESPAÑOL! Is your child wild about nature? The Arboretum is the natural place to celebrate a birthday.

item.title: OVERFLOW RADIO: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation
item.description:
Saturday, October 3, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks – Gallery @ MATCH, 3400 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

October 3-24, 2026DiverseWorks Gallery @ MATCHGallery Hours: 12 noon – 6 pm, Thursday-Saturday Celebrated for her large-scale social choreographies, Emily Johnson / Catalyst’s newest project, Overflow Radio is a performance, skill-share, planting of 1000 trees, and radio transmission from across territories. In conjunction with the world premiere of Overflow Radio in Mni Sóta Makoce (Minneapolis), DiverseWorks hosts an Overflow Radio: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation here in Houston. Over 24 non-consecutive hours, we will gather in-person to listen to twelve First Nations and Indigenous authors, poets, and scholars live-broadcasting from their home territories and First Nations. We’ll pay attention to other scales, other forms, other knowledges. We’ll traverse together, transcending colonial borders, languages and time. We’ll feast and celebrate the making of community, as we practice our shared commitment to creating our possible futures, as we gather what we need to know. The program is developed in collaboration with Emily Johnson and local Indigenous and Native artists to include talks, skill-shares, listening gatherings, an exhibition, and performances by Aveda Adara, Chiara Beaumont, Chichi, Karen Navarro, Aryn Ward and Monica Villarreal, with additional participating artists and community partners to be announced. The project is co-organized by DiverseWorks, Emily Johnson / Catalyst, and the participating artists and partners. Programs (please check back for updated information)DW Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS: Emily Johnson, 6:30 pm July 29Opening Event and Reception: 5 – 8 pm, October 3Listening Gatherings: 12noon – 6 pm (specific hours TBD), October 9-12Diverse Discourse Lecture & Studio Visits: Mary Bourdeaux: October 16-19 / Lecture 6 pm, Oct. 17 AcknowledgementsOverflow Radio is a National Performance Network Creation & Development Fund Project commissioned by Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater (REDCAT) and co-commissioned DiverseWorks, MASS MoCA and University of Minnesota Department of Theatre Arts & Dance, more information at www.npnweb.org. Overflow Radio is developed through creative residencies provided by MASS MoCA, John and Mabel Ringling Museum of Art, Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater, University of Minnesota’s Imagine Fund with support from the McKnight Foundation, and Danspace Project with support from the New York State DanceForce, a partnership program of the New York State Council on the Arts. Overflow Radio is created with generous support from First Peoples Fund, Howard Gilman Foundation, Harkness Foundation for Dance, and the New England Foundation for the Arts’ National Dance Project with lead funding from the Doris Duke Foundation and The Mellon Foundation. Emily Johnson / Catalyst is fiscally sponsored by Producer Hub. Image: Emily Johnson / Catalyst, Quilt Being Star, worn by Ty Fierce Matteba, photo by Two Hawks Young.

From DiverseWorks

item.title: Inprint Ayad Akhtar Reading
item.description:
Monday, October 5, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Alley Theatre, 615 Texas Avenue, Houston, TX, 77002

General admission tickets will go on sale on Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Ayad Akhtar will read from his new novel The Radiance, followed by an on-stage conversation led by a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Pulitzer Prize winner Ayad Akhtar’s new novel The Radiance is “simply put, a work of genius. Through unforgettable characters Akhtar explores the nature of memory and of the soul, while the unfolding tale builds tension and anticipation like a whodunit” (Abraham Verghese). It has been named one of the New York Time‘s “Novels Everyone Will Be Talking About in 2026.” A mysterious accident along a country road sparks an awakening and an investigation in Akhtar’s most daring work yet—a visionary novel of spiritual transformation in an age of fracture. Akhtar’s work as a novelist and playwright has been published and performed in over two dozen languages. He is the winner of the Pulitzer Prize for Drama for his play Disgraced, which was also nominated for the Tony Award for Best Play. His other Broadway plays include McNeal, Junk, and The Who & The What. Akhtar is also the author of the novels American Dervish, a Kirkus Reviews Best Book of the Year, and Homeland Elegies, called “a tour de force” by The Washington Post. In 2021, he was named the New York State Author by the New York State Writers Institute, succeeding Colson Whitehead.

From Inprint Houston

item.title: Succulent Pumpkin Workshop Oct 9-10
item.description:
Friday, October 9, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: Brookwood Gift & Garden Center & Café, 1502 FM 1489, Brookshire, TX, 77423, United States

Brookwood Horticulture Workshop: Succulent Pumpkin Centerpiece A Fall Favorite You Won’t Want to Miss! Autumn is calling—and so are the pumpkins! Join us for one of Brookwood’s most beloved seasonal traditions: the Succulent Pumpkin Centerpiece Workshop, led by Horticulture GM Robert Grove. In this hands-on experience, you’ll blend the rich textures of fall with the fresh beauty of succulents to craft a one-of-a-kind centerpiece that’s perfect for your table—or to gift to someone special! 🍂 What’s Included: Create & Take: Design your very own succulent pumpkin masterpiece to take home and enjoy all season long. Expert Guidance: Learn arrangement tips and care techniques from Brookwood’s own horticulture pro, Robert Grove. Flexible Scheduling: Choose from 10 sessions over two days—making it easy to fit into your busy fall calendar. Celebrate the beauty of the season with friends, creativity, and purpose—surrounded by the plants grown and cared for by the incredible Citizens of Brookwood®. 📍 Hosted at Brookwood Gift & Garden Center🌟 Let your fall décor tell a story of creativity, community, and heart. Dates: Friday & Saturday, October 9 & 10, 2024 Time: Choose from Five Sessions Each Day: 9-10 AM 10:15-11:15 AM 11:30 AM-12:30 PM 1-2 PM 2:30-3:30 PM Location: Horticulture Building, Behind the Garden Center Registration: $45 (plus tax) covers all the materials needed to make your own centerpiece. Space is limited, so reserve your spot today! Grab your tickets today!   Dining Options: Lunch at The Brookwood Café: Available Friday and Saturday from 11 AM – 2 PM. Lunch reservations are required and can be made here: https://bit.ly/BWOpenTable Please note: Food is not included with the event ticket.   Join us for an inspiring afternoon of horticultural know-how, flavorful food, and a purposeful take-home gift! Reserve your spot today! When you’re in the checkout cart, please click the “ORDER NOTE” option to let us know if you’d like to sit with specific guests. Be sure to include their names so we can arrange seating accordingly. Please note that our luncheon tables seat up to 8 guests.   Thank you for supporting the beloved adults with disABILITIES who live and work at Brookwood! Changing the way the world thinks about adults with disabilities Visit our Events Calendar for the full schedule of Brookwood’s upcoming events.   CANCELLATION POLICY: Full Refund (100%): Requests made 7 or more days before the event date will be eligible for a full refund. Partial Refund (50%): Requests made between 6 days and 48 hours before the event date will be eligible for a 50% refund. item.title: Inprint Hernan Diaz Reading
item.description:
Monday, October 12, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Stude Concert Hall, Rice University, Entrance #18 & #20, 6100 Main St., Houston, TX, 77005, United States

General admission tickets will go on sale on Monday, September 21, 2026 at 12 pm. Season tickets are on sale here. Hernan Diaz will read from his new novel Ply, followed by an on-stage conversation led by a local author/journalist. The evening will conclude with a book sale and signing. The event is presented as part of the 2026/2027 Inprint Margarett Root Brown Reading Series.  Described by Lauren Groff as a “narrative genius,” Hernan Diaz is the Pulitzer Prize-winning and bestselling author of the novel Trust, named one of the New York Times’s Best 100 Books of the 21st Century and currently being developed as a limited series for HBO. His literary work is celebrated for its genre-bending reinvention of American mythology and its complex exploration of wealth, capitalism, and isolation. His first novel, In the Distance, was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize and the PEN/Faulkner Award. His work has been translated into 37 languages. After rewriting America’s past in his two previous novels, from 1920s Wall Street to the 19th century western frontier, Diaz turns to the future with his new novel Ply. A combination of Dickensian odyssey, family drama, and scientific thriller, Ply examines the place of technology in the American imagination. Centuries from now, the state has been dismantled, and humans are reinventing social bonds and learning new ways to coexist with nature. Following a childhood defined by loss, survival, and found family, an orphan grows up to become a “pincher,” someone who steals electricity from the grid to sell it on the black market. “Diaz brilliantly envisions how love, trust, and loyalty can remain when freedom and justice have collapsed and makes every page exhilarating and meaningful” (Library Journal, starred review).

From Inprint Houston

item.title: ESCRITORES EN LA CASA: Ezequiel Zaidenwerg
item.description:
Thursday, October 15, 2026 at 7:30 PM

Location: Inprint House, 1520 W Main St, Houston, TX, 77006, United States

Inprint recibe al autor argentino Ezequiel Zaidenwerg para presentar su nueva novela en verso, Fantasma escritor. Tras la presentación, Zaidenwerg conversará sobre su obra con un escritor local. Esta presentación forma parte de la serie de Inprint Escritores en la casa. Todas las presentaciones de Escritores en la casa son gratis y están abiertas al público.  Ezequiel Zaidenwerg nació en Buenos Aires en 1981. Es autor de varios libros incluyendo los poemarios Doxa (2007) y La lírica está muerta (2011, 2017). Además, es traductor de Mark Strand, Ben Lerner, Anne Carson, Weldon Kees, Robin Myers, Joseph Brodsky, Mary Ruefle, João Cabral de Melo Neto,  Brenda Hillman, Kay Ryan y Emily Dickinson, entre otros y otras. Es miembro fundador del colectivo de acción poética Como Un Lugar y envía diariamente por mail poemas traducidos a través de su newsletter El poema de hoy. Su primera novela, Fantasma Escritor, fue elogiada por Fernanda Trías, quien escribió: “Ezequiel Zaidenwerg dirige su inteligencia inquieta hacia los fantasmas que nos constituyen: la familia, la lengua, el duelo, el deseo, la herencia. Zaidenwerg, que con su newsletter El poema de hoy ha hecho de la poesía y la traducción una forma de encuentro colectivo, entrega ahora una primera novela íntima y luminosa, vulnerable y formalmente viva. Este es un libro sobre la traducción como una manera de estar en el mundo: el arte de escuchar aquello que nos rodea y de encontrar las palabras que acaso nos permitan decir yo.” Esta serie de lecturas es posible gracias a la Rita Mallett Blasser Foundation

From Inprint Houston

item.title: Inprint Cool Brains! Series presents Elizabeth Acevedo
item.description:
Sunday, October 18, 2026 at 2 PM

Free and open to the public Free copies of Anger Is Only a Shadow for the first 100 families Appearance by celebrated Houston writer Jasminne Mendez Meet the author followed by a book sale and signing Bus scholarships available for student groups – full scholarships for public schools, partial scholarships for private schools upon availability. For information, email info@inprint.org Books available through Kindred Stories And more! The 2026/2027 Inprint Cool Brains! Series proudly presents National Book Award winner and renowned poet Elizabeth Acevedo, sharing her new YA novel Anger Is Only a Shadow. Known for YA novels filled with poetry, humor, and heart, Elizabeth Acevedo is the New York Times-bestselling author of The Poet X, which won the National Book Award for Young People’s Literature, the Michael L. Printz Award, the Pura Belpré Award, the Carnegie medal, the Boston Globe–Horn Book Award, and the Walter Award. She is also the author of With the Fire on High, which was named a best book of the year by the New York Public Library, NPR, Publishers Weekly, and School Library Journal; and Clap When You Land, which was a Boston Globe–Horn Book Honor book and a Kirkus finalist. Acevedo is a National Poetry Slam Champion and served as the 2022 Young People’s Poet Laureate. “An irresistible story of family connection, resilience, and loyalty” (Kirkus starred review), Anger Is Only a Shadow is Acevedo’s powerful new YA novel in prose and poetry. Lil is anything but small. She’s rebellious, she’s loyal; she’s figuring out what kind of good person she wants to be, or if she wants to be a good person at all. But more than anything? Lil wants to be free. When her instinct for freedom leads to another stay in D.C. juvenile detention, Lil knows she’s lucky to just be on probation. But judgment, guilt, and an ankle monitor weigh heavily on her, and she can’t shake that pinned-down feeling. The only person who might understand is her big brother, Aldwin. Except he’s more distant now than just the hundred miles from his college. As her court hearing ticks closer, a question looms over Lil as the missed phone calls and strange texts from her brother pile up: will she stay put, or put her future freedom on the line? “A striking and nuanced portrait of the realities of juvenile detention and mental illness” (Publisher’s Weekly starred review) and “intensely genuine” (The Bulletin of the Center for Children’s Books starred review), Anger Is Only a Shadow a white-knuckle journal to self-understanding and doing the right thing, no matter the cost.

From Inprint Houston

item.title: Park to Port Bike Ride
item.description:
Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: Bayou Parkland, 6532 Almeda Rd, Houston, TX, 77021, United States

Hermann Park Conservancy’s 12th annual Park to Port Bike Ride is set for Saturday, October 24. The 20-mile round-trip bike ride takes cyclists from Hermann Park’s Bayou Parkland along the Bayou Greenway trail all the way to Mason Park, near the Port of Houston. Enjoy the turn-around party, but be sure to save some energy for a well-deserved post-ride party under the Bill Coats Bridge! Park to Port is open to riders of all skill levels and is not a race. Whether you are an experienced cyclist or are riding just for fun, you can go at your own pace on this scenic city journey. Your participation in Park to Port supports Hermann Park Conservancy and its stewardship efforts for one of Houston’s most beloved parks while promoting the ever-growing Bayou Greenway trail system. Register and learn more at the following link: 12th Annual Park to Port Bike Ride. Early bird pricing is available until August 17. SPECIAL OFFER: Save $10 on registration when you sign up for BOTH the Park to Port Bike Ride and Run in the Park! Bundle deal is available via the link above. Information on Run in the Park can be found here.

From Hermann Park Conservancy

The season concludes on November 6–8, 2026 in Houston, Texas, with a $50,000 Invite-Only Championship featuring 128 of the best players in the game. Points Leaderboard – Top performers across all events Total Spots: 64 3. LCQ Winners – Winner of each Last Chance Qualifier (16 events) Total Spots: 16 If a player qualifies through multiple methods, leaderboard spots roll down to the next eligible player. Bonus for the Most Consistent Players The Top 8 players on the final Points Leaderboard earn a Round 1 Bye at the Invitational.
